docs\index.md:7:SWE-bench is a benchmark for evaluating large language models on real world software issues collected from GitHub. Given a *codebase* and an *issue*, a language model is tasked with generating a *patch* that resolves the described problem.

docs\reference\harness.md:3:This section documents the Docker-based evaluation harness for SWE-bench.
docs\reference\harness.md:7:The SWE-bench evaluation harness uses Docker containers to create reproducible environments for evaluating model-generated patches on software repositories. This containerized approach ensures consistent evaluation results across different platforms and eliminates environmental discrepancies.
docs\reference\harness.md:9:The `swebench.harness` module provides the main evaluation infrastructure for SWE-bench tasks. This module is responsible for setting up Docker environments, applying patches, running tests, and determining if the patches resolve issues.
docs\reference\harness.md:13:There are two important scripts in the `swebench.harness` module:
docs\reference\harness.md:15:- `swebench.harness.prepare_images`: This script can be used to build Docker images for task instances
docs\reference\harness.md:16:- `swebench.harness.run_evaluation`: This script is used to run the evaluation of a prediction file
docs\reference\harness.md:18:In general, you don't need to run `prepare_images` unless you're specifically interested in building Docker images locally. `run_evaluation` is the main script you'll use to run evaluations for all task instances in the SWE-bench datasets.
docs\reference\harness.md:22:The harness operates in three main layers:
docs\reference\harness.md:34:This layered architecture allows for efficient caching and reuse of common components while ensuring isolated evaluation for each task.

docs\reference\harness.md:42:3. **Test Execution**: Run the repository's test suite
docs\reference\harness.md:43:4. **Grading**: Determine if the patch resolves the issue

docs\faq.md:5:### What is SWE-bench?
docs\faq.md:7:SWE-bench is a benchmark for evaluating large language models on real-world software engineering tasks. It consists of GitHub issues and their corresponding fixes, allowing LLMs to be evaluated on their ability to generate patches that resolve these issues.
docs\faq.md:9:### Which datasets are available?
docs\faq.md:11:SWE-bench offers five main datasets:
docs\faq.md:13:- **SWE-bench**: The full benchmark with 2,294 instances
docs\faq.md:14:- **SWE-bench Lite**: A smaller subset with 300 instances
docs\faq.md:15:- **SWE-bench Verified**: 500 instances verified by engineers as solvable
docs\faq.md:16:- **SWE-bench Multimodal**: 100 _development_ instances with screenshots and UI elements (test eval is on [the SWE-bench API](https://www.swebench.com/sb-cli).)
docs\faq.md:17:- **SWE-bench Multilingual**: 300 instances spanning 9 languages and 42 repositories
docs\faq.md:19:### How does the evaluation work?
docs\faq.md:21:The evaluation process:
docs\faq.md:23:1. Sets up a Docker environment for a repository
docs\faq.md:25:3. Runs the repository's test suite
docs\faq.md:26:4. Determines if the patch successfully resolves the issue
docs\faq.md:32:- **Total instances**: Number of instances in the dataset
docs\faq.md:34:- **Instances completed**: Number of instances that completed the evaluation process
docs\faq.md:35:- **Instances resolved**: Number of instances where the model's patch fixed the issue
docs\faq.md:36:- **Instances unresolved**: Number of instances where the evaluation completed but the issue wasn't fixed
docs\faq.md:38:- **Instances with errors**: Number of instances where the evaluation encountered errors
docs\faq.md:58:You can also set `--cache_level=env` and `--clean=True` when running `swebench.harness.run_evaluation` to only dynamically remove instance images after they are used. This will make each run longer, but will use less disk space.

docs\guides\datasets.md:1:# SWE-bench Datasets
docs\guides\datasets.md:3:SWE-bench offers multiple datasets for evaluating language models on software engineering tasks. This guide explains the different datasets and how to use them.
docs\guides\datasets.md:7:SWE-bench provides several dataset variants:
docs\guides\datasets.md:11:| **SWE-bench** | Full benchmark with diverse repositories | 2,294 instances | Comprehensive evaluation |
docs\guides\datasets.md:12:| **SWE-bench Lite** | Smaller subset for quick evaluations | 534 instances | Faster iteration, development |
docs\guides\datasets.md:13:| **SWE-bench Verified** | Expert-verified solvable problems | 500 instances | High-quality evaluation |
docs\guides\datasets.md:14:| **SWE-bench Multimodal** | Includes screenshots and UI elements | 100 dev instances (500 test) | Testing multimodal capabilities |
docs\guides\datasets.md:15:| **SWE-bench Multilingual** | 9 programming languages, 42 repositories | 300 instances | Cross-lingual evaluation |

.\docs\openclaw-setup.md:35:> **Note:** Tamp is [open source (MIT)](https://github.com/sliday/tamp). You can audit the source, build from git, or run from a local clone instead of npm: `git clone https://github.com/sliday/tamp && cd tamp && npm install && node bin/tamp.js -y`

.\README.md:14:End-to-end token optimizer for Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, and OpenAI Codex CLI. Compresses bash output up to **95%**, collapses redundant calls, and injects a terse prompt persona — automatically, with zero new runtime dependencies.
.\README.md:20:Three methods — all produce the same result (binary at `~/.claude/squeez/bin/squeez`, hooks registered).

.\README.md:36:# Or run once without installing
.\README.md:45:cargo install squeez
.\README.md:54:`squeez setup` auto-detects every CLI present on disk and registers the hooks. `squeez uninstall` removes them. Session data and `config.ini` are preserved so reinstall is lossless.

.\README.md:62:| **Codex CLI** | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` | ✅ native | ✅ native | 🟡 soft via `AGENTS.md` | `apply_patch` hooks landed in 0.123.0 ([#18391](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/18391)); `updatedInput` + `read_file`/`grep` hook surface still pending ([openai/codex#18491](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/18491)) |

.\README.md:99:| **Bash compression** | Intercepts every command via `PreToolUse` hook, applies smart filter → dedup → grouping → truncation. Up to 95% reduction. |
.\README.md:102:| **Adaptive intensity** | Truly adaptive: **Full** (×0.6 limits) below 80% of token budget, **Ultra** (×0.3) above. Used to be always-Ultra; now actually responds to session pressure. |
.\README.md:103:| **MCP server** | `squeez mcp` runs a JSON-RPC 2.0 server over stdio exposing 13 read-only tools so any MCP-compatible LLM can query session memory directly. Hand-rolled, no `mcp.server` dependency. |
.\README.md:104:| **Auto-teach payload** | `squeez protocol` (or the `squeez_protocol` MCP tool) prints a 2.4 KB self-describing payload — the LLM learns squeez's markers and protocol on first call. |
.\README.md:105:| **Caveman persona** | Injects an ultra-terse prompt at session start so the model responds with fewer tokens. |
.\README.md:106:| **Memory-file compression** | `squeez compress-md` compresses CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / copilot-instructions.md in-place — pure Rust, zero LLM. i18n-aware: set `lang = pt` (or `--lang pt`) for pt-BR article/filler/phrase dropping and Unicode-correct matching. |
.\README.md:108:| **Token tracking** | Every `PostToolUse` result (Bash, Read, Grep, Glob, Monitor, SubagentStop) feeds a `SessionContext` so squeez knows what the agent has already seen. Read/Grep/Glob/Monitor outputs are also rewritten via `updatedToolOutput` (Claude Code v2.1.119+) when content is redundant or oversized. |
.\README.md:109:| **Token economy** | Sub-agent cost tracking (~200K tokens/spawn), burn rate prediction (`[budget: ~N calls left]`), session efficiency scoring, tool result size budgets. |
.\README.md:110:| **Auto-calibration** | `squeez calibrate` runs benchmarks on install and generates an optimized `config.ini` (aggressive / balanced / conservative profiles). |
.\README.md:116:squeez optimizes what it can reach — the surfaces exposed by each host's hook API. It cannot fix token leaks outside those surfaces.
.\README.md:123:| **Read / Grep / Glob limits** | `PreToolUse` injects `limit` / `head_limit` per `read_max_lines` / `grep_max_results` | Every Read/Grep/Glob call | Claude Code, Copilot, OpenCode (hard); Gemini + Codex soft via GEMINI.md / AGENTS.md |
.\README.md:124:| **Read / Grep / Glob / Monitor output rewrite** | `PostToolUse` runs `squeez compress-output` and returns `updatedToolOutput` when content is redundant or oversized | Claude Code v2.1.119+ | Claude Code |
.\README.md:125:| **Agent / Task prompt** | `PreToolUse` compresses `tool_input.prompt` (markdown-aware, via `compress-prompt`) | When prompt > `agent_prompt_max_tokens` | Claude Code (post–v1.8.0) |
.\README.md:126:| **Sub-agent output** | `SubagentStop` hook feeds `last_assistant_message` into SessionContext for cross-call dedup | On every sub-agent completion | Claude Code |
.\README.md:127:| **Compaction lifecycle** | `PreCompact` logs the event; `PostCompact` emits a re-arm reminder so the model knows compression is still active | On context compaction | Claude Code |
.\README.md:133:**Agent/Task returned output.** No hook API surface exists to rewrite an Agent's return value. `PostToolUse updatedToolOutput` (Claude Code v2.1.119+) covers built-in tools (Read, Grep, Glob, Monitor) but not the Agent/Task result. Workaround: keep agent prompts compact (squeez compresses at dispatch time via PreToolUse), and use `squeez_agent_costs` MCP tool to monitor spawn overhead.
.\README.md:135:**Skills & slash-command files.** Claude Code loads these into the system prompt before any hook fires. squeez has no visibility into session-start system prompt construction.
.\README.md:139:**Tools whose host doesn't expose PreToolUse / BeforeTool.** E.g. Codex `apply_patch` hooks landed in 0.123.0, but `updatedInput` is explicitly unsupported and `read_file`/`grep` still have no hook surface ([openai/codex#18491](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/18491)) — so Read/Grep caps for Codex are soft hints in AGENTS.md, not hard injections.

.\README.md:430:### Hooks (Claude Code & Copilot CLI)
.\README.md:432:Six hooks work together automatically after install on Claude Code (three on Copilot CLI):
.\README.md:436:- **`PostToolUse`** — tracks every tool result; rewrites Read/Grep/Glob/Monitor output via `updatedToolOutput` when content is redundant or oversized (Claude Code v2.1.119+)
.\README.md:437:- **`SubagentStop`** *(Claude Code only)* — feeds `last_assistant_message` into SessionContext so the parent agent can dedup against what the sub-agent saw
.\README.md:438:- **`PreCompact`** *(Claude Code only)* — logs compaction events for session efficiency metrics; allows compaction to proceed
.\README.md:439:- **`PostCompact`** *(Claude Code only)* — emits a re-arm reminder after compaction so the model knows compression is still active
.\README.md:451:**Fuzzy match** — bottom-k MinHash over whitespace-token trigrams (k=96, Jaccard ≥ 0.85, length-ratio guard ≥ 0.80). Survives timestamp changes, added/removed blank lines, and single-line edits. Collapses to:
.\README.md:483:Plugin installed at `~/.config/opencode/plugins/squeez.js`. OpenCode auto-loads plugins on startup. All Bash commands are automatically compressed via `squeez wrap`.
.\README.md:497:TypeScript extension installed at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/squeez/index.ts`. Pi auto-discovers extensions from that directory — no settings patching needed. Session memory is injected via a skill at `~/.pi/agent/skills/squeez/SKILL.md`; Pi includes the skill description in every system prompt and loads full instructions on demand. Unlike other hosts, Pi achieves `BUDGET_HARD` output compression via the `tool_result` event (return-patch API), not just soft hints.
.\README.md:512:bash bench/run.sh           # filter-mode benchmark (14 fixtures)
.\README.md:513:bash bench/run_context.sh   # context-engine benchmark (3 wrap scenarios)
.\README.md:514:./target/release/squeez benchmark   # full 19-scenario benchmark suite
.\README.md:516:bash build.sh               # build + install to ~/.claude/squeez/bin/
.\README.md:532:CI runs `cargo test`, `bench/run.sh`, `bench/run_context.sh`, and `squeez benchmark` on every push and pull request.

.\README.md:12:**Open-source LLM gateway written in Rust.**
.\README.md:15:[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
.\README.md:23:Edgee is a lightweight LLM gateway that sits between your application and AI providers. It gives you a single control point for routing, observability, and cost optimization, without changing your existing code.
.\README.md:25:Think of it as an open-source alternative to LiteLLM or OpenRouter, written in Rust for speed and low resource usage, with a built-in token compression engine that reduces your AI costs automatically.
.\README.md:27:<img width="1997" height="807" alt="ai-gateway-horizontal-light" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d68ff91d-a488-428e-b99d-f4e1c3ef9242" />
.\README.md:32:- **One gateway, any provider** — Unified API for Anthropic, OpenAI, and other LLM providers. Switch models without touching your app code.
.\README.md:33:- **Token compression** — Edgee analyzes request context and strips redundancy before it reaches the model. Same output, fewer tokens, lower bill.
.\README.md:34:- **Real-time observability** — See exactly how many tokens you're sending, how many you're saving, and what it costs.
.\README.md:44:curl -fsSL https://edgee.ai/install.sh | bash
.\README.md:50:brew install edgee-ai/tap/edgee
.\README.md:56:irm https://edgee.ai/install.ps1 | iex

.\README.md:84:edgee launch codex resume         # resume the last Codex session
.\README.md:90:If you'd rather type `claude` (or have another tool spawn `claude` for you), install Edgee's shims:
.\README.md:93:edgee alias            # installs all three; pass `claude`, `codex`, `opencode` to scope
.\README.md:100:2. Writes executable shim scripts to `~/.edgee/bin/{claude,codex,opencode}` and prepends `~/.edgee/bin` to `PATH` in the same rc block. This means **non-interactive** shells — including `bash -c '...'`, scripts, and tools that spawn Claude Code via `exec` — also get routed through Edgee. Reopen your terminal (or `exec $SHELL -l`) once after install.
.\README.md:102:### Use as a standalone gateway
.\README.md:107:# Start the gateway
.\README.md:110:# Your app talks to Edgee instead of the provider directly
.\README.md:118:### Token compression
.\README.md:120:Edgee's compression engine analyzes tool outputs (file listings, git logs, build output, test results) and removes noise before they enter the LLM context. The compression is lossless from the model's perspective — responses are identical, but prompts are leaner.
.\README.md:122:### Multi-provider routing
.\README.md:124:Route requests across Anthropic, OpenAI, and other providers through a single endpoint. Switch models, load-balance, or failover without code changes.
.\README.md:128:Real-time visibility into token consumption, compression savings, and cost per request.
.\README.md:134:When you run `edgee launch claude`, Claude Code shows a live statusline with the current session's token usage and compression savings. **No setup required** — the first launch auto-installs the integration into `~/.claude/settings.json`, and subsequent launches reuse it.
.\README.md:139:edgee statusline claude install   # run the install manually (idempotent)
.\README.md:146:The install writes two things to `~/.claude/settings.json`:
.\README.md:153:- `statusline-claude.installed` — set after the first auto-install; gates repeats.
.\README.md:154:- `statusline-claude.disabled` — set by `disable`; tells the launch flow to skip auto-install too.
.\README.md:158:Claude Code only renders **one** `statusLine`, picked by strict precedence: enterprise > project `.claude/settings.local.json` > project `.claude/settings.json` > user `~/.claude/settings.json`. Any project that defines its own `statusLine` (via project hooks, in-house scripts, or third-party statusline tools) will completely shadow Edgee's user-level statusline.
.\README.md:168:`edgee statusline claude fix` writes a `statusLine.command` of the form `edgee statusline wrap '<original>'` into `.claude/settings.local.json` (per-user, gitignored). The shared `.claude/settings.json` is **never** touched. Each Claude Code refresh then runs Edgee's renderer and the wrapped command in parallel and merges their outputs into a single line.
.\README.md:172:The `SessionStart` hook installed by `edgee statusline claude install` (or by the auto-install on first launch) prints a single warning line whenever the current project's statusLine shadows Edgee, and stays silent otherwise.
.\README.md:192:| Claude Code | `edgee launch claude` | ✅ Supported |
.\README.md:193:| Codex | `edgee launch codex` | ✅ Supported |
.\README.md:202:The token compression engine in Edgee is derived from [RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk), created by [Patrick Szymkowiak](https://github.com/pszymkowiak) and contributors at rtk-ai Labs. RTK pioneered local tool-output compression for AI coding assistants, and we built on their work to bring the same optimizations to a gateway architecture.
.\README.md:204:RTK is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. All derived files retain the original copyright notice and are individually marked with a modification history. See [`LICENSE-APACHE`](./LICENSE-APACHE) and [`NOTICE`](./NOTICE) for full details.
.\README.md:206:If you're looking for a local-first compression tool, [check out RTK directly](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk), it's excellent for individual developer workflows.
